title: `isError`
description: The in-band flag marking a tool result as a tool execution error, which the spec expects clients to pass to the model so it can correct itself.
question: Can the agent tell a tool execution error from a successful result?
notes: Pydantic AI surfaces the failure through a different channel; the OpenAI Agents SDK loses it entirely. 3 cannot reach the revision.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI 1.15.1 requires MCP Python SDK 1.26.x, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 requires mcp<2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.3: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0: a result flagged `isError` is returned as an ordinary text output with no error signal. The agent cannot distinguish it from a successful call.
notes_by_num.4: Pydantic AI 2.40.0: the failure is raised as a `ModelRetry` carrying the error text. The agent learns the call failed, but through an exception that prompts a retry rather than through the result's error flag.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra 1.17.3 negotiated MCP 2025-11-25. The scanner refused to compare that capture with a 2026-07-28 source.

verdict.headline: Visible in Pydantic AI through a changed channel, invisible in the OpenAI Agents SDK.
verdict.detail: This is the most consequential split in the result boundary. On Pydantic AI 2.40.0 a failed tool call raises `ModelRetry`, so the agent reacts. On OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0 the same call returns the error text as a normal success, so an agent can act on a failure believing it worked. CrewAI, LangChain and Mastra cannot negotiate MCP 2026-07-28, so they reach none of it.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: MCP separates protocol errors from tool execution errors precisely so a model can retry the second kind with better arguments. A framework that raises both as exceptions, or reports both as success, collapses that distinction and removes the recovery path the spec designed.
